nodes_add.name: Godavari Mataji
nodes_add.note: Sati Godavari Mataji of Sakori; arrived 1924 aged 10; named Upasni's successor (Hinduism Today); led the Kanya Kumari Sthan after 1941. Dates 1914-1990 from Wikipedia and a Cafoscari interview title; Hinduism Today gives none.

nodes_update.note: Kashinath Govind Upasni; b. 15 May 1870 Satana; d. 24 Dec 1941 Sakori. Settled at Sakori 1917, 1918 or 1922 depending on source; Meher Baba Trust chronology has Merwan visiting him at Sakori in 1916-17.
Ramalingam; b. 5 Oct 1823 Marudur; vanished 30 Jan 1874 Mettukuppam by followers' account. Death is a faith claim.
b. 9 Jul 1918 Machilipatnam; d. 22 Mar 2007 Vallecrosia (memorial compilation gives 22 Mar 2.30 pm; Wikipedia cites The Hindu of 25 Mar 2007, the likely origin of the '25 March' date).

edges_upsert.note: Reached Shirdi late June 1911; more than a year in the Khandoba temple; ordered worshipped by Sai Baba on Guru Purnima 1913.

Met at Khandoba temple, Shirdi, Dec 1915 (Meher Baba Trust chronology); about seven years of association; addressed as Avatar end of Dec 1921 per Purdom, The God-Man p. 26; last meeting Dahigaon 17 Oct 1941 per Kalchuri, Lord Meher p. 2724.

Per Hinduism Today (Aug 1992) she arrived 1924 aged 10 and at 18 received mantra initiation and a rudraksha mala and was named spiritual successor; year 1932 is computed from those ages, so approximate.
Hymns on Shiva and Muruga in the Nayanar tradition; he also criticised orthodox ritual and was attacked by Arumuga Navalar.
Vethathiri (1911-2006) said to be inspired by Ramalinga Swamigal (Wikipedia, citing Aiyasamy 2019 and New Indian Express 2012); no personal contact possible.
Heard talks from 1947, direct dialogue from 1953, break after a heated exchange; 1967 Saanen events; argued against him afterwards.
Raised in a Theosophist household; worked in Leadbeater's library from 1941; joint general secretary of the Indian section; left early-to-mid 1950s.

glossary.def: The 'pure true path' taught by Vallalar: compassion for all living beings, worship of God as a light of grace, and a goal of a transformed, deathless body.
Compassion for all living beings, Vallalar's central ethic, shown above all in feeding the hungry and refusing to kill animals.
'Supreme Grace-Light', Vallalar's name for God and the first word of his mantra.
'Poems of Divine Grace', the roughly 5,800 poems of Vallalar in six books.
The community of unmarried women founded by Upasni Maharaj at Sakori, trained in Sanskrit and Vedic ritual.
U.G. Krishnamurti's name for the condition he said remained after thought stopped interpreting experience. He offered no method for reaching it.
